title: GPipe: Pipeline Parallelism for Giant Networks
hook: Spread a network's layers across accelerators as pipeline stages, then split each batch into micro-batches so no accelerator sits idle — near-linear speedup for giant models.
key_points: Partitions a sequence of layers across accelerators as pipeline stages.
A novel batch-splitting (micro-batch) algorithm keeps all accelerators busy for near-linear speedup.
Demonstrated a 557M-parameter AmoebaNet reaching 84.4% top-1 on ImageNet.
content_html: Yanping Huang, Youlong Cheng, Ankur Bapna, and colleagues at Google introduced GPipe, a pipeline-parallelism library for networks that can be expressed as a sequence of layers. It partitions those layers across accelerators as stages, then uses a micro-batch pipelining scheme to keep every accelerator working. They used it to train a 557M-parameter AmoebaNet to 84.4% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet and a 6B-parameter, 128-layer Transformer across more than 100 languages.
extra_html:
How it works

GPipe assigns consecutive groups of layers to different accelerators, forming a pipeline of stages. The catch with naive pipelining is that stages stall waiting for each other, so GPipe splits each mini-batch into smaller micro-batches that flow through the pipeline together. With several micro-batches in flight at once, the accelerators stay busy and the method reaches near-linear speedup.

Why it matters

Pipeline parallelism lets a model grow deeper than any single accelerator's memory allows, and GPipe made it practical with the micro-batch trick. Its results span both vision and language — the AmoebaNet ImageNet result and the multilingual 6B Transformer — showing the approach is general. (Its exact arXiv title is "GPipe: Efficient Training of Giant Neural Networks using Pipeline Parallelism".)

related.title: Megatron-LM: Training LLMs with Model Parallelism
related.hook: Split the big matrices inside attention and MLP layers across GPUs, add a few communication ops, and you can train an 8.3B model on 512 GPUs — no custom compiler needed.

related.title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations for Trillion-Parameter Models
related.hook: Data-parallel training wastes memory by copying optimizer states, gradients, and parameters onto every GPU. ZeRO partitions them instead — fitting 100B+ parameter models.
